newsitem.title: USA: Browning-Ferris gets HK trash contract.
newsitem.headline: Browning-Ferris gets HK trash contract.

text.p: Browning-Ferris Industries Inc said on Tuesday that Hong Kong's Environmental Protection Department granted Swire BFI Waste Services Ltd a contract to design, build and operate seven waste transfer stations.
The contract is valued at US$41.5 million to build the facilities and about US$5.75 million per year to operate them for 15 years, Browning-Ferris said.
Swire BFI is a company jointly owned by Swire Pacific Ltd and Browning-Ferris.
The contract calls for construction of a network of seven mini-stations on different islands to serve scattered island communities, Browning-Ferris said.
The outlying island network of transfer stations will handle up to 610 tonnes of waste a day as well as waste water and sewage sludges and construction wastes, the company said.
The first four stations will be built to begin operation in mid-1998 and the remaining three will follow, Browning-Ferris said.
Waste at the stations will be compacted and sent by container vessels to the West New Territories Landfill, the company said.
